title: Compatible Noetherian proper models carrying an invertible module
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with $X$ affine, and let $M$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. There exist a small nonempty directed partially ordered set $I$ with a least element $0$, an inverse system of proper morphisms $f_i:Y_i\to X_i$, transition morphisms $q_{ji}:Y_j\to Y_i$ and $r_{ji}:X_j\to X_i$ for $j\geq i$, and projections $a_i:Y\to Y_i$ and $b_i:X\to X_i$, with the following properties. All transition morphisms and projections are affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism]; $f_iq_{ji}=r_{ji}f_j$ and $f_i a_i=b_i f$. The cones $(Y,a_i)$ and $(X,b_i)$ are limits: every compatible cone from a scheme $T$ to either system factors uniquely through its displayed cone. Each $X_i$ is affine and of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Each $X_i$ and $Y_i$ is Noetherian (locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]), and $Y_i$ is quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. There is an invertible module $M_0$ on $Y_0$ and an isomorphism $a_0^*M_0\cong M$. For $M_i=q_{i0}^*M_0$, every $M_i$ is invertible, $q_{ji}^*M_i\cong M_j$, and $a_i^*M_i\cong M$, with the isomorphisms induced by pullback composition [def-pc-module-pullback].

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], the affine scheme $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Apply the affine-base clause of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-limit-noetherian] to $f$. Write its small nonempty directed indexing set as $K$, its models as $f_k:Y_k\to X_k$, its transitions as $q_{lk},r_{lk}$, and its limit projections as $a_k,b_k$. Each $X_k$ is affine and of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, each $f_k$ is proper, both systems have affine transitions, and both cones are limits. The approximation gives $f_kq_{lk}=r_{lk}f_l$ and $f_ka_k=b_kf$. No finite-presentation hypothesis on the original $f$ is introduced.

source.place: Tag 0D2S, lemma-ample-in-neighbourhood, first approximation paragraph; limits.tex Tag 0A0P, lemma-proper-limit-of-proper-finite-presentation-noetherian, with the affine-base clause of its cited DAG statement.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], every $X_k$ is Noetherian, since it is of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. Properness includes finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism], so apply the same Noetherian permanence statement to $f_k$ to deduce that $Y_k$ is Noetherian. Thus both are locally Noetherian and quasi-compact. By [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated], every $Y_k$ is quasi-separated. These supply all the stage hypotheses for invertible-module descent.

source.place: Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian; properties.tex Tag 01OY, lemma-locally-Noetherian-quasi-separated; morphisms.tex Tag 01W1, definition-proper.

proof.text: Apply clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-limit-cone-affine-projections-opens] to each of the two limit cones from step 1. Since both systems have affine transitions, every $a_k:Y\to Y_k$ and $b_k:X\to X_k$ is affine. This verifies the projection clause separately from the transition clause of approximation.

source.place: Tag 01YX, lemma-directed-inverse-system-has-limit, clause (1), applied to the two given limit cones.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-invertible-affine-limit-descent] to the $Y_k$ system and $M$. The index set is small, nonempty and directed, the stages are quasi-compact and quasi-separated by step 2, the transitions are affine by step 1, and $Y$ is their scheme limit. Obtain $c\in K$, an invertible $\mathcal O_{Y_c}$-module $N$, and an isomorphism $a_c^*N\cong M$.

source.place: Tag 0B8W, lemma-descend-invertible-modules, clause (2), invoked in Tag 0D2S immediately after approximation.

proof.text: The order $\le$ on $K$ is a preorder: write $k\sim l$ when $k\le l$ and $l\le k$. Choose one representative in each $\sim$-class, taking $c$ itself as the representative of its own class, and let $K'\subseteq K$ be the set of chosen representatives. On $K'$ the induced order is a partial order, since two equivalent representatives are equal, and $K'$ is cofinal in $K$, since every $k$ is $\le$ its representative. Restrict to $I=\{k\in K'\mid k\geq c\}$, with $c$ labelled $0$. This is a small partially ordered set with least element $c$; it is directed and cofinal in $K$: given $k,l\in K$ choose $m\geq k,l,c$ in $K$ and replace $m$ by its representative. Here is the limit check, for either scheme system $Z_k$. Given a compatible cone $t_i:T\to Z_i$ over $I$, for arbitrary $k\in K$ choose $l\in I$ with $l\geq k$ and set $t_k=Z_{lk}t_l$. For two choices $l,l'\in I$, choose $m\in I$ with $m\geq l,l'$; compatibility gives $Z_{lk}t_l=Z_{mk}t_m=Z_{l'k}t_{l'}$. Thus the extension is independent of the choice, is compatible with all transitions of $K$, and is the unique extension of the tail cone. The original limit property gives its unique map to $Z$. Hence the restricted cones with vertices $Y$ and $X$ are still limits. All stage properties, affine transitions and affine projections persist: they are the same schemes and maps at the retained indices. Put $M_0=N$ on $Y_0=Y_c$.

source.place: Tag 0D2S, lemma-ample-in-neighbourhood, sentence After shrinking I; elementary directed-tail cone argument, written out here.

proof.text:
For $i\in I$ define $M_i=q_{i0}^*M_0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-invertible] every $M_i$ is invertible. The composition isomorphisms explicitly supplied by [def-pc-module-pullback], together with $q_{i0}q_{ji}=q_{j0}$ and $q_{i0}a_i=a_0$, give
$$q_{ji}^*M_i=q_{ji}^*q_{i0}^*M_0\cong q_{j0}^*M_0=M_j,\qquad a_i^*M_i\cong a_0^*M_0\cong M.$$
At the least index identify $q_{00}^*M_0$ with $M_0$ by the identity-pullback isomorphism of the same definition. These are the required isomorphisms induced by pullback composition. Together with the proper models, commutative squares and limit properties already established, this gives every clause of the statement.

Step 2: Noetherian stages via finite-type-over-noetherian applied twice (properness includes finite type), and Y_k quasi-separated via locally-noetherian-quasi-separated. Step 3: projections are affine by limit-cone-affine-projections (1). Step 4: every hypothesis of invertible-affine-limit-descent holds. Step 6: invertibility via invertible-pullback-invertible (Lean-closed), and the isomorphisms via the composition and identity isomorphisms of def-pc-module-pullback, using q_{i0}q_{ji}=q_{j0} and q_{i0}a_i=a_0. The item requires a partially ordered I with least element 0, and the step asserted this for the tail {k>=c} without argument. FIX: step 5 now chooses one representative per class of k<=l<=k, keeping c as its own representative (Categories remark-preorder-versus-partial-order). It shows the set of representatives is partially ordered and cofinal, and restricts the extension argument to I = representatives >= c. No module changes because c is kept. Edge cases checked: X empty (A=0, singleton system), M=O_Y, non-Noetherian A and f not of finite presentation (never used).
